    Proportion of heterogeneity explained by predictions

    Source: R/yardstick-metrics.R
    heterogeneity_r2.Rd

    heterogeneity_r2() is a yardstick numeric metric that measures how much of the between-study heterogeneity a model explains. The total heterogeneity \(\tau^2_0\) is the DerSimonian-Laird estimate for the observed effect sizes. The residual heterogeneity is the matching moment estimate around the predictions, \(\tau^2_r = \max\{0, (Q_r - (k - 1)) / (\sum w_i - \sum w_i^2 / \sum w_i)\}\) with \(Q_r = \sum w_i (y_i - \hat y_i)^2\) and \(w_i = 1 / v_i\). Both estimates use the same scaling, so predicting the weighted mean for every study gives 0 and perfect predictions give 1. The metric is \(\max(0, 1 - \tau^2_r / \tau^2_0)\), the out-of-sample analogue of the pseudo \(R^2\) of meta-regression (Raudenbush, 2009). It is NA when there is no heterogeneity to explain.

    Usage

    heterogeneity_r2(data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
heterogeneity_r2(
  data,
  truth,
  estimate,
  variance,
  na_rm = TRUE,
  case_weights = NULL,
  ...
)

heterogeneity_r2_vec(
  truth,
  estimate,
  variance,
  na_rm = TRUE,
  case_weights = NULL,
  ...
)

    Arguments

    data

    A data frame with the columns given in truth, estimate and variance.

    ...

    Not currently used.

    truth

    <data-masking> Observed effect sizes.

    estimate

    <data-masking> Predicted effect sizes.

    variance

    <data-masking> Sampling variances. For the _vec() function, a numeric vector.

    na_rm

    A logical value indicating whether NA values should be stripped before the computation proceeds.

    case_weights

    Not supported. Must be NULL.

    Value

    A tibble with columns .metric, .estimator and .estimate. heterogeneity_r2_vec() returns a single number between 0 and 1.

    See also

    Other meta metrics: coverage_prob(), inverse_var_rmse()

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg
)
fit <- meta_regress(bcg, ~ ablat)
bcg$pred <- predict(fit, newdata = bcg)$.pred
heterogeneity_r2(bcg, .yi, pred, variance = .vi)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   .metric          .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr>            <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 heterogeneity_r2 standard       0.832
